title: Pantry
summary: Food and gear for at least 2 weeks at home, the Red Cross figure for home. Food your household already eats, that needs no fridge and little or no cooking or water.

items.text: Non-perishable food your household eats, for at least 2 weeks
items.note: Choose food that needs no refrigeration, little or no cooking and little or no water. Keep some that is ready to eat, even if most of it needs cooking.

items.text: Ready-to-eat canned meats, fish, poultry, beans, fruits, vegetables, pasta and soup
High-energy foods: peanut butter, nuts, jerky, trail mix, protein or fruit bars
Dry cereal or granola, and crackers
Dried fruit and canned juices
Milk that keeps on the shelf: powdered, canned or shelf-stable boxes
Staples: sugar, salt, pepper, instant coffee, tea bags, cocoa
Comfort foods, such as hard candy and chocolate bars
Foods your children already eat
items.note: A disaster is not the time to surprise young children with new foods.

items.text: Food for anyone with a special diet, allergies or a medical need, and for older people
Vitamin and mineral supplements
Baby supplies: formula, bottles and baby food, if you have a baby
items.note: Never buy or use infant formula after its Use-By date.

items.text: Pet food, if you have pets
Manual can opener
Paper plates, cups, plastic utensils and paper towels
Food-grade containers that close tightly: glass jars with screw-top lids, heavy plastic or metal
items.note: For opened packages and for keeping out insects and rodents.

items.text: Zipper-closure plastic food storage or freezer bags
Marker, to date food when you buy it and when you open it
Cooking directions or mix ratios written on cards, for staples not in their own package
A written list of meals for each day for 14 days, with the water and gear each needs
Appliance thermometers for the fridge and freezer, and a food thermometer
A cooler and frozen gel packs
Extra cooking fuel for 2 to 4 weeks
items.note: Charcoal grills and camp stoves are for outdoor use only. Where and how to cook safely is in Cook without power; storing fuel is in Store fuel safely.

items.text: Drinking water, as on the Home water store list
items.note: Plan extra for food that needs water, such as dry milk, dried soups, instant rice and freeze-dried food.
